title: AI robots in our homes – level 3
paragraphs: Big technology companies are investing heavily in humanoid robotics, and racing to bring AI from screen interfaces into physical homes and workplaces.

Meta recently developed a prototype humanoid named Max in just three months. They want to provide a physical body for its digital AI assistant. Proponents argue that building robots with human-like form allows them to navigate spaces, handle tools, and use infrastructure designed specifically for people. However, tech critics argue that current AI remains unreliable for real-world physical tasks. Human environments present unpredictable challenges and make delicate interactions such as handling fragile household objects extremely difficult to execute safely. Furthermore, developing autonomous home assistants requires gathering vast amounts of spatial data. This raises major cybersecurity concerns regarding surveillance, data privacy, and potential hacking risks.

While researchers work on advanced 3D spatial mapping to help machines navigate rooms, experts remain divided over whether consumer humanoid robots are an inevitable step forward or an overhyped financial gamble.
